title: Maximum Number of Occurrences of a Substring
statement: Consider every substring of `s` whose length is at least `minSize` and at most `maxSize`, and which uses no more than `maxLetters` different letters. Among those substrings, find the one that appears in `s` the most times and return how many times it appears. Occurrences are counted at every starting position, so two occurrences may overlap. If no substring meets the rules, return `0`.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
signature: int maxFreq(String s, int maxLetters, int minSize, int maxSize)
notes:
## Intuition

The brute force counts every substring of every length from `minSize` to `maxSize`. The key observation is that `maxSize` does not matter. If a longer substring occurs `k` times, its first `minSize` letters also occur at least `k` times, and that shorter piece cannot use more different letters than the longer one. So the best count is always reached by some substring of length exactly `minSize`, and one window of that fixed size can slide across `s`.

## Approach

1. Keep `letters`, a map from each letter in the window to how many times it appears, and `counts`, how often each valid window string was seen.
2. Move `right` across `s`, adding `s[right]` to `letters`.
3. The window is `s[left..right]` with `left = right - minSize + 1`; skip until `left` reaches 0.
4. If the window has at most `maxLetters` distinct letters (`letters.size`), add one to its string's count in `counts` and update `best`.
5. Remove `s[left]` from `letters` (deleting the key when it reaches zero) so the window can slide.
6. Return `best`, which stays `0` if no window qualified.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "aababcaab"`, `maxLetters = 2`, `minSize = 3`. The windows are `"aab"`, `"aba"`, `"bab"`, `"abc"`, `"bca"`, `"caa"`, `"aab"`. `"abc"` and `"bca"` have 3 different letters and are skipped. The others are counted, and the second `"aab"` raises its count to 2, so `best = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · minSize): each of the n windows is copied and hashed once, and `minSize <= 26`.
- Space: O(n · minSize) for the stored window strings.

## Pitfalls

- Trying every length up to `maxSize` is correct but wasteful; only `minSize` can win.
- Occurrences may overlap (`"aaa"` appears twice in `"aaaa"`), so slide one step at a time.
- Delete a letter from `letters` when its count drops to zero, or `letters.size` will overstate the distinct letters.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `letters` | letter → count inside the current window |
| `counts` | window string → number of valid occurrences |
| `best` | highest count seen so far |
| `left`, `right` | first and last index of the window |
| `incoming`, `outgoing` | letter entering and leaving the window |
| `word`, `times` | the window's text and its updated count |

narration.8: Count the new letter inside the window.
narration.9: The window always has exactly minSize letters, so its left edge follows from the right one.
narration.10: The first window is not full yet.
narration.13: Only windows with few enough different letters count.
narration.14: Copy the window's text so equal windows share a key.
narration.15: One more occurrence of this text.
narration.19: The leftmost letter is about to leave the window.
narration.20: Its last copy is leaving, so it no longer counts as a distinct letter.
narration.26: The best count over all windows of length minSize is the answer.
